title: Delving into Topology Representation for Layout Pattern: A Novel Contrastive Learning Framework for Hotspot Detection
problem: Machine learning-based layout hotspot detection struggles to capture decision boundaries across entire datasets and ignores geometric/topological properties of polygons.
motivation: Lithographic hotspot detection is critical for yield at advanced nodes, but geometric complexity of layout patterns is not captured by existing ML approaches.
method: CLI-HD: contrastive learning framework operating on layout sequences and images; Layout2Seq encodes polygon shapes as vectors within sequences; absolute position embedding replaces standard Transformer positional encodings to capture topology.
key_novelty: First contrastive learning framework explicitly encoding geometric and topological polygon information for hotspot detection.
contributions: CLI-HD contrastive learning framework for layout hotspot detection
Layout2Seq: polygon-to-vector encoding for geometric representation
Absolute position embedding for topology-aware attention
0.82%-4.77% accuracy improvement; 4.9%-23.18% false alarm rate reduction
limitations: Test datasets and specific lithography nodes not specified; scalability to diverse pattern families not discussed.
primary_theme: Topology-aware contrastive learning for lithographic hotspot detection
